card.title: What reset actually moves
card.blurb: `--soft`, `--mixed` and `--hard` move your branch to exactly the same place. Watch where each one leaves the files the undone commit was holding.
hero.title: What reset actually moves
intro.0: You commit something you did not mean to, and the word `reset` starts to sound like a command that deletes your work. It is calmer than that, and it is not one outcome but three. Every reset moves your branch's name back to a commit you name; what changes is where the files from the undone commit end up - still staged, back in the folder, or gone. Watch all three side by side, so you can pick the one you actually meant.
concept.gt-reset.def: Moving your branch's name to another commit, with a choice of what happens to the files you had staged or edited.
step.0.narr:
Three commits, and `main` on the newest. That last one is the mistake: Pip's feeding time went into `feeding.md` and was committed before anyone had checked it, under the message `oops`.

It is saved now - the panel shows the last commit holding all three lines. Staging and the folder are empty, because everything is committed.
step.0.note: `main` sits on the commit you wish you had not made.
step.1.narr:
`git reset --soft HEAD~1` moves `main` back one commit. The `oops` dot is still drawn, but no name points at it any more.

Pip's line did not travel back with the name. The panel has opened on `Staging` and put a dot on it, because that copy differs from the one behind it: `+ Pip 08:00`, sitting there, still picked for the next commit you make. **The snapshot went; the work did not.**
step.1.note: `--soft` - the name moved back, the work waits in staging.
step.2.narr:
Run the same step back with `--mixed`, and `main` lands on **exactly the same commit**. Compare the graph with the last step: it is identical.

The panel has moved one button to the left. The same `+ Pip 08:00`, now in the working tree and picked for nothing, so you choose again what goes into the next commit.
step.2.note: `--mixed` - same move, the work waits in the folder.
step.3.narr:
`--hard` makes that same step back and keeps nothing. Staging is empty, the folder is empty, and the panel falls back to the last commit - Mia and Rex, no Pip.

The line you were holding is in no zone at all now. This is the one to read twice before you run it.
step.3.note: `--hard` - same move, and the work is gone.
step.4.narr:
The graph move was identical all three times. The mode only ever decided where Pip's line came to rest.

That is what makes `--soft` useful: the work is still staged, so one `git commit` puts it straight back under the message you meant. Pick the mode by deciding where you want the files waiting for you.
step.4.note: Reset moves a name. The mode decides where your work lands.
legend.0: working tree - the file as it is right now
legend.1: staging - the copy you picked for the next commit
